faqs: What is NCLEXBase?

NCLEXBase is an online resource that will fully prepare you for the NCLEX-RN®. We have:

  • 2,600+ NCLEX® Questions, vague like the real exam
  • 50 NCLEX® Cases with video explanations
  • Crash Course Videos covering the most tested concepts
  • 4 Readiness Exams that predict your chances of passing
  • 140+ Printable Cheat Sheets to master must-know NCLEX® topics
  • Study Schedule Creator to create your own personalized study schedule
  • Pass Targets Tracker to know exactly when you’re ready
  • Next Gen NCLEX® Strategy Course to teach you about the Next Gen NCLEX®
  • Ask NCLEXBase AI to instantly answer your content questions
  • 4.9+ ★ Rated Mobile App available on iOS and Android.
  • And an NCLEX® Pass Guarantee!
I'm already using another NCLEX® question bank. How is NCLEXBase different?

The Next Gen NCLEX® is an updated test, and you need to prepare with an updated question bank. NCLEXBase is the only nursing resource created specifically for the Next Gen NCLEX®.

The Next Gen change means that the test now requires clinical judgment, and you can’t develop clinical judgment just by reading explanations alone. Instead, our video case walkthroughs and our Next Gen strategy course teach you how to think like a nurse and how to prioritize, which are the most important skills you need for NCLEX® success. Our question bank gives you plenty of opportunity to practice those skills.
Does NCLEXBase have a pass guarantee?

No, and we would be careful of anyone who offers one. No prep site sits in the exam room with you, and no amount of practice makes a result certain.

What we do instead is make sure the exam is not the first time you have seen a question written the way the NCLEX® writes them. There are free questions in every subject, so you can judge the material before you pay for any of it.
Can I use NCLEXBase for the NCLEX-PN®?

The question bank is written for the NCLEX-RN®. The NCLEX-PN® tests highly similar content with differences mainly in scope of practice, so most of the material transfers — but it is not written for the PN specifically, and you should know that before you buy.
Is NCLEXBase updated for the 2026 NCLEX® test plan changes?

Yes. Every Next Generation item type is in the question bank — matrix, bowtie, drag-and-drop cloze, drop-down, highlight, select-N, select-all-that-apply and multiple choice — and questions are written against the 2026 NCLEX-RN® Test Plan.
Does NCLEXBase have a study guide or study schedule?
Yes. Open Study Schedule once you are signed in and set your exam date; the plan is built around it and adapts as you work through it. The Study Guide page covers what to study and in what order.

While you review a test you can tag each question as learning, reviewing or mastered. The tags are yours: they let you build a later test from only the questions you have not got on top of yet, instead of working through everything again.

performance: Your score is calculated based on the result of every question you attempt. You can answer each question as many times as you’d like. Every correct answer will increase your average score.
Can I reset my score for each subject?
Not at the moment. However, you can answer each question as many times as you’d like. Every correct answer will increase your average score.
Can I reset or untag my used questions?
Not at the moment. Once a question is used, it remains used. However, you can answer each question as many times as you'd like and change the tag each time.
Are Case Studies and Readiness Exam included in my performance?
Yes, Case Studies and Readiness Exam scores and questions used are included.
readiness: What are the CAT Readiness Exams?

They're practice exams that simulate the real NCLEX experience. They use computerized adaptive testing (CAT), the same method the NCLEX uses to pick questions. Use them to gauge your readiness to pass the NCLEX!
How does computerized adaptive testing work?

The real NCLEX uses a scoring algorithm to pick the next question based on your performance. Answer correctly and the next question tends to be slightly harder; miss one and the next question tends to be slightly easier.
Why did my exam shut off at 85 questions?

Each exam has at least 85 questions and at most 150, just like the real NCLEX. The exam stops once it can tell with confidence whether you're above or below the passing standard, or when you reach 150. Stopping at 85 doesn't mean you passed or failed. It means the exam had enough information to decide. Your result is shown on the results screen.
What does my Chance of Passing result mean?

Your result (Low, Borderline, High, or Very High) is based on how you performed across all the questions you got. One exam is a snapshot, a pattern across several exams is a much better predictor. If you score High or Very High on several exams, that's a strong sign you're ready. This is practice feedback, not a guarantee of your NCLEX result.
Are CAT exams harder or easier than the real NCLEX?
The exams are built to match the real NCLEX's content, format, and difficulty. Since both tests adapt to you, they should feel about equally hard.
When should I take my first CAT Readiness exam?

Take an exam at the start of your studying to identify strengths and weaknesses. Practice with the question bank, then take another exam midway through your studying and another before the NCLEX to reassess your readiness. If you follow the study schedule, it’ll tell you exactly when to take the exams.
Can I pause, go back, or change an answer?

You can pause and resume an exam at any time, but we recommend completing it in one sitting if possible. Once you submit an answer, you cannot go back or change it. The real NCLEX works the same way, and the adaptive system needs your answers to be final to choose your next question.
schedule: Why should I use the study schedule creator?

Students who use a study schedule score higher than those that don’t. But PDF study schedules are rigid and annoying to use. So we took our proven NCLEX® study schedule PDF and turned it into an interactive customizable calendar!
  • Select your start and exam date, and the schedule creator will create a personalized study schedule for you.
  • Easily customize your schedule by adding days off, moving assignments, or changing your exam date.
  • If you fall behind, click rebalance and the schedule creator will evenly distribute your overdue assignments up to your exam date.
This schedule will help you stay organized and on track to exam day. Create a personalized schedule today and get started!
I already started the PDF schedule. How can I switch to the study schedule creator?

You can still use the study schedule creator even if you’ve started the PDF schedule!
  1. Create a schedule with today as your start date.
  2. Mark all the assignments you've already done as complete.
  3. Then click Rebalance, and the study schedule will evenly spread your remaining assignments up to your exam date.
The study schedule will evenly distribute your remaining assignments up to your exam date like magic!
Is this the same as the PDF study schedule?
Yes — same assignments, same order. We recommend the schedule creator rather than a printed sheet, because it fits the plan to your own exam date and you can move it when life happens.
What if I fall behind or need to change something?

No worries, you can click rebalance and the schedule creator will evenly distribute your overdue assignments up to your exam date. You can move assignments, take days off, adjust your study speed, or change your exam date. You’re in full control.
